applies_why: The judge text does not weigh a pressing side's own chain against a live link by footing; it treats the challenged curse limb as dropped and therefore no live link to contradict.
quote: C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: pressed against a link: whether it means any link ever pressed or only a live link; I read it as requiring a live link, so the rule does not apply to this dropped-limb disposition.
why: The judge disposes of C4 because the defender dropped the challenged curse limb, leaving no live link to contradict, so it neither weighs a live pressed link chain-against-chain nor applies the retired stating-verse test.
